title: Prefill servo: adaptive kernel scheduling and interleaved-replay safeguards
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Multi-stream CUDA Graph captures during prefill + decode have intermittent nondeterminism when kernel candidates and capture boundaries change under load. We've observed subtle divergences on long-sequence workloads and during mixed-quant runs where replay produces different memory alignment and occasional OOMs. Goal: implement a lightweight 'prefill servo' subsystem that adapts kernel selection and capture window boundaries at runtime to keep captures idempotent and reduce capture churn, while preserving latency SLOs.

Scope and approach: 1) Servo controller: a runtime agent (servo) that monitors per-stream sequence-length distribution, active kernels, and occupancy signals, and selects a stable kernel candidate set per capture-epoch (capture-epoch = contiguous prefill->decode window). The servo must only change kernel choices at safe epoch boundaries to avoid mid-capture drift. 2) Capture-epoch watermark: define a compact epoch token propagated to CUDA Graph captures; replay checks epoch token compatibility and rejects replay if incompatible (fall back to eager kernels). 3) Interleaved-replay safeguards: when multiple streams share a device, allow the servo to coordinate a micro-quiesce (<= 2ms) to align prefills for streams that would otherwise produce conflicting kernel bindings. The micro-quiesce is configurable and gated by SLO and load. 4) Deterministic kernel probe: a small deterministic probe kernel runs at capture time to validate memory layout/quantization path before committing the graph. If the probe fails, the capture aborts and a fallback path is used, with telemetry for post-mortem.

Acceptance criteria: - No increased tail latency beyond configured micro-quiesce budget (default 2ms) for 95% of requests. - Nightly fuzz harness with 10k mixed-length sessions shows <0.01% replay divergence compared to baseline. - Rollout: feature gated; opt-in flag per deployment; can be disabled by customers.

Design docs and artifacts: design doc: drive.redwood/runtime/prefill-servo-v1 (internal), prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8921, fuzz harness: infra/replay-fuzz/nightly/servo-harness, perf dashboard: grafana.redwood/runtime/servo-prefill-2026.

Tradeoffs and notes: - Conservative epoch boundaries reduce capture churn but may slightly increase memory footprint because we hold KV caches a bit longer. - Micro-quiesce helps correctness but can add transient latency spikes under heavy contention — we will start with a conservative 2ms default and expose a per-customer knob. - Deterministic probe adds a tiny overhead to capture; probe runs only during new capture commits (not on replay).
updates: 2026-01-20 - Asha Kapoor: Created ticket after two customer incidents where mixed-quant decode diverged on replay. Attached initial telemetry and request traces.

2026-01-28 - Liam O'Connor: Spike complete: implemented proof-of-concept servo that chooses kernel candidates based on measured per-batch occupancy. Found one race where kernel list was mutated during capture; added epoch lock in PoC.

2026-02-05 - Priya Nair (QA): Added fuzz harness case: 5k sessions, mixed lengths 8-4096, with quantization toggles. Observed 0.12% divergence when servo changed kernel mid-epoch. Repro linked: github.com/redwood-inference/replay-fuzz/issue/124.
2026-02-14 - Liam O'Connor: Decided to add capture-epoch watermark and probe step. Updated design doc with watermark proto and probe semantics. Opening prototype PR: runtime#8921.
2026-02-27 - Engineering sync notes: micro-quiesce default set to 2ms; ops request circuit-breaker if quiesce rate > 0.5% over 5m. Performance and SLO owners to validate on dedicated pools first.
2026-03-03 - Performance benchmarks: on n4-large-mixed benchmark, 95p latency increased by 0.9ms with quiesce enabled; token throughput unchanged. Added regression alert threshold in grafana panel.
2026-03-09 - Security review: team confirmed no customer data exfil risk; probe kernel limited to device-local memory reads. Marked security_review_required=false.

2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Merged prototype behind feature flag on canary infra. Starting controlled rollout to 'dedicated-alpha' cluster and running 24h stability sweep. Next: expand fuzz coverage and add automatic rollback on divergence spikes.
